chunks: And from him (Al-Hurr al-Amili) from Al-Nadr from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to pray Friday prayer when the sun had passed its zenith by the length of a shoelace, and he would deliver the sermon in the first shadow; then Gabriel (peace be upon him) would say, 'O Muhammad, the sun has set (passed zenith), so descend and pray.' And Friday prayer was made only two rak'ahs because of the two sermons, so it is a prayer until the Imam descends (to lead the congregation).
And from him (Al-Hurr al-Amili) from Al-Nadr from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The time for Friday prayer is at the zenith (zawal), and the time for Asr prayer on Friday is the same as the time for Dhuhr prayer on other days, and it is recommended to hasten (pray early) with it.

key_terms.التَّبْكِيرُ: Hastening or performing the prayer early within its time
key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: The zenith of the sun, marking the start of Dhuhr and Jumu'ah times
key_terms.الْخُطْبَتَيْنِ: The two sermons delivered before the Friday prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: Two units of prayer, specific to Friday prayer in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed time for Friday prayer and how does it differ from regular days?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the precise timing of Jumu'ah prayer, linking it to the Prophet’s practice of praying immediately after solar zenith while the Imam delivers the sermons in the shade. It establishes the theological rationale for the two-rak'ah structure, attributing it to the inclusion of the two khutbahs, and aligns the Friday Asr time with the standard Dhuhr window, emphasizing the virtue of hastening the prayer (tabkir).
